prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Houston for AC repair?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” HVAC shop for everyone — the right company depends on your location in Houston, how quickly you need service, whether it’s a simple repair or system replacement, your budget, and whether you want brand-certified technicians or special warranties. That said, here are reputable options and how to choose the best one for you.

Well-regarded Houston options (good starting points)
- Baker Brothers Plumbing & Air — Houston-based, long-standing local reputation for AC service and installs, good for residential repairs and warranties.
- John Moore Services — large local company offering 24/7 emergency service and a broad service area in Houston.
- ARS/Rescue Rooter (and related franchise brands like Rescue Rooter/ARS) — national company with local presence, offers emergency and maintenance plans.
- Aire Serv / Neighborly-branded contractors — franchise network with local contractors; often offers flat-rate pricing and service agreements.
- Horizon Services (in Texas markets) — known for financing options and service agreements.

How to pick the best one for your situation
- Verify licensing and insurance: Texas HVAC contractors should be registered and insured.
- Check current reviews: Google, Yelp, and BBB for the most recent service experiences in your neighborhood.
- Ask about certifications: NATE-certified techs and factory certifications (Carrier, Trane, Lennox) indicate training.
- Compare written estimates: get 2–3 quotes for repairs or replacements and compare parts, labor, and warranties.
- Inquire about warranties: parts vs. labor vs. system warranties and any required maintenance to keep warranties valid.
- Emergency availability and response time: if it’s summer and your AC’s out, rapid availability matters.
- Fees: ask about diagnostic fees, after-hours surcharges, and whether the diagnostic fee is applied to repairs.

Key questions to ask when you call
- Are you licensed/registered in Texas and insured?
- What are your diagnostic fee and how long before a technician can arrive?
- Do your techs have NATE or manufacturer certifications?
- What’s the estimated cost range for this problem and do you offer a written estimate?
- What parts and labor warranties do you offer?
- Do you offer emergency/after-hours service and what are the fees?
- Can you provide references or recent reviews from customers in my neighborhood?

Red flags to avoid
- Very low upfront price without an explanation — could be bait-and-switch.
- Techs unwilling to explain diagnosis or show the faulty parts.
- No written estimate or no warranty on work.
- High-pressure sales tactics for a full replacement before trying repairs (unless replacement truly recommended).

If you want, tell me your Houston ZIP code or neighborhood and whether this is an emergency repair or a planned service/replace — I can look up highly rated local companies and current reviews in your exact area.
